item.title: FMD | First private vet authorised to help with vaccinations
item.description: A private veterinarian from the Mossel Bay district is the first in the country to be authorised to assist a state veterinarian with the vaccination of animals against foot-and-mouth disease (FMD). A further 100 applications from private veterinarians have already been submitted.

item.title: Peanut butter recalled over aflatoxin
item.description: Certain ButtaNutt peanut butter products have been recalled at the manufacturer’s request after aflatoxin levels exceeded the legal limit.

item.title: WATCH | One million FMD vaccine doses arriving in SA on Saturday
item.description: One million doses of Argentine vaccine will arrive in South Africa tomorrow, Saturday 21 February, Agriculture Minister John Steenhuisen announced earlier this month.

item.title: ‘We cannot put entire cattle herd under quarantine’ – SA dairy industry demands FMD policy clarity
item.description: Manufacturers of dairy products still have no clarity on how unprocessed milk from healthy cows that have been preventively vaccinated against foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) should be handled. Cheese production is one of the potential problem areas.

item.title: From our editor: Farmers are burying their future while government watches
item.description: This week, I depart from my usual column format to write what is, in essence, an open letter to the President of South Africa, Cyril Ramaphosa, the Minister of Agriculture, John Steenhuisen, and all nine provincial MECs responsible for Agriculture, Rural Development and Land Reform.

item.title: Free FMD training for farmers by Agri Studies and Agri Auctions
item.description: Two agricultural organisations are providing South African farmers with free training on foot-and-mouth disease (FMD) prevention and outbreak response to help protect livestock assets and maintain market access during the current FMD crisis.

item.title: Steenhuisen ‘seriously concerned’ about provisional liquidation application for Tongaat Hulett
item.description: John Steenhuisen, minister of agriculture, has now also voiced his serious concerns for the South African sugarcane value chain following recent news that the sugar milling giant, Tongaat Hulett, is likely to be placed under provisional liquidation.

item.title: Temperatures drop, but early frost unlikely
item.description: As the western parts of the country experienced extremely hot conditions over the past few days, weak cold fronts elsewhere caused minimum temperatures to drop to about 10°C. Farmers wondered whether the first frost of the year may be on its way.

item.title: WATCH | Cost of FMD vaccines – ‘Now is not the time to make a profit,’ says Steenhuisen
item.description: Farmers who want to vaccinate their herds against foot-and-mouth disease early, once enough doses are available in the country, will pay between R45 and R80 per animal, depending on the supplier. “We’ve been very clear with Onderstepoort Biological Products that we’re in a crisis and this is not an opportunity to make a profit.”
